title: GREENER COMPOSITE STRUCTURES USING RECYCLABLE AND BIOBASED MATERIALS FOR OUT OF AUTOCLAVE PROCESS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To demonstrate the efficiency of sustainable and biobased resin to produce recyclable, repairable and reusable composite parts compliant with space requirement by out of autoclave process. Description:  The environmental impact of space activitiesis receiving increasing attention across the European space sector. In line with ESA's Ecodesign Policy, future missions are expected to assess their environmental footprint through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodologies and identify solutions that reduce resource consumption, energy usage, waste generation, and hazardous materials. Composite manufacturing processes have been identifiedas a relevant environmental hotspot, notably during the preparation of the EcoStar IOD mission (ESA PrepE 24-P-M-OPS-12), where out-of-autoclave manufacturing using sustainable feedstocks was highlighted as a promising mitigation pathway. At this stage most of the resins are made using petroleum-based feedstock material and the market is mostly led by non-European large entities. Some of the chemical used to produce most of the resins (i.e Bisphenol A) are subject to increasing regulatory scrutiny and may face future restrictions under the European REACH framework, highlighting the need for sustainable and readily available alternative materials. In this work, sustainable European sourced feed stock material shall be used to produced thermosetting resin to be used in combination with carbon fibres to enable composite part manufacturing by out of autoclave process that will exhibit recyclable, repairable and reusable capabilities. This includes extended pot life resin, 100% biobased resin, REACH compliant resin and vitrimer-based resin. Composites based on carbon fibre will be produced using sustainable resin and tested to reach TRL 4 first at sample level and thenat breadboard level representative of existing mature design for space. The activity will also assess the environmental benefits of the proposed materials and processes through LCA, comparing them against conventional composite manufacturing approaches. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of the different out of autoclave processes existing for space applications, - - - - - - Review of the commercially available sustainable resins that could be used for out of autoclave processes, Performing a trade-off taking into account materials/processes compatibility, sustainability aspect of the resin, capability to enable composite recycling, reuse and repairability Select at least 2 different out of autoclave processes for further investigation, Development of test plan at sample level to assess the performance of the chosen material and process, Design, produce and test 2 demonstrators based on relevant composite parts for space applications, Perform simplified LCA and Ecodesign trade off and selection.Deliverables:Breadboard, Report

title: T811-902SD ADVANCED IN-SITU DATA PROCESSING FOR SPACE DEBRIS MODEL VALIDATION (EXPRO+)
description: The knowledge on the small space debris population is still limited. Large debris populations are welldocumented,with ground radarand telescopes cataloguing objects >10 cm in Low Earth Orbit and 30-40 cmin Geostationary Orbit. Debris in the cm to sub-cm range remains largely uncharted, relying on statisticalsampling via remote sensing, in-situ detectors and retrieved space-exposed hardware. Due to their highvelocities, small debris impacts are a threat to sensitive spacecraft equipment (panels, de-orbitingmechanisms,exposed payloads) and human life. Space debris models, used for risk assessment, rely oncollected samples to model small debris.Several recent space missions carried detectors, with data being collected more often than before. However,there is still no unifiedway to neither collect nor process these efficiently for the output quantities (flux, objectmass/diameter, velocity, source) to beincluded in a model. With the advances in technology and big datahandling, acquisition, storing and efficient processing becomes more realistic.This activity aims to develop a software that can ingest, store and process in-situ measurements of spacedebris. Itwill produce quantities that can be ingested without modifications in the validation toolchain of a spacedebris model. The measurements should include in-situ impact datasets, focusing on the widely usedpiezoelectric and plasma detectors. The inclusion of in-situoptical data and data from photographic surveyswill be considered. A standardised format, compatible with the needs of space debris models, will be ensured.The development of a conversion tool will be part of the main retrieval and processing software or shall resultin a stand-alone tool that can handle the output of the main software.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs  RD  Entities. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: COMPACT LASER SYSTEMS FOR ALKALI RYDBERG ATOMIC SENSORS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a low SwaP breadboard of a full laser system that will manipulate Rydberg atom in vapour cell, and be able tobe configured for sensing applications for RF receivers.Description: Highly-excited atoms, often known as Rydberg atoms, display extreme sensitivity to external electromagnetic (EM) fields, including the electric fields associated with black-body radiation (BBR).In addition to their use in quantum computing, Rydberg atoms can be configured for sensing applications. Such sensors make use of non-destructive read-out of Rydberg states, which is implemented optically, including fluorescence detection of low-lying Rydberg states. A range of different Rydberg sensing modalities have been developed; these include those developed for microwave standards andimaging in the Terahertz regime to sensitive digital communications techniques in radio and microwave bands. This activity developsa complete laser system needed to perform an RF instrument based on Alkali Rydberg Atomic Sensors. To do so the selection of the relevant parameters to address the sensor is aimed to be done by consolidating the first set of requirements. A dedicated focus is to be addressed towards a low SWaP (Size, Weight and Power) for CubeSAT platform. This shall ensure a proper design and manufacturing of the Laser system. This breadboard is then tested on an adequate Rydberg sensor for RF measurement. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement review for laser system to manipulate Rydberg atom - Design of a compact laser system - Manufacturing of the laser system - Test on Rydberg Atom and validation of the RF instrument.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
